title: Quay Street's pillar box: the target (cloud week 42, 9 October 2026, second try)
revision: second try, after TARGET-REVIEW.md (FAIL on F1, the height, and nine narrow points N1 to N9, all applied)

units.length: millimetres in this file unless a key says metres (_m)
units.frame: origin on the box's vertical axis at the footway surface; +y is the FRONT (the door and slot side); +x is to the viewer's right when looking at the front; z up
units.pivot: the axis at the footway surface (z = 0): the pivot of the .glb; the hidden skirt runs to z = -150
units.kinds: Read (printed in the repository), Derived (computed), Judgement (the writer's choice; basis 'Memory' where it rests on general knowledge of the type). Scaled and Photo are EMPTY: no drawing and no photograph of a pillar box was reached.

summary_line: Quay Street's pillar box is a cast-iron cylinder of the 1950s-60s standard 'Type A' pattern, painted pillar-box red (sRGB 150/30/32) above a black base band 200 mm high: body 489 mm across, a 576 mm foot, a 560 mm cap with a shallow 80 mm dome, 1500 mm above the footway in all (the research's working figure; the stand-in's 1612 is 0.11 m too tall), a 320 x 45 mm letter slot centred at 1278 mm under a 30 mm hood, a 300 x 888 mm door (flush: 1 mm proud, a joint groove round it, hinged on the left with no hinge showing; a keyhole escutcheon and one collection-plate frame) and, where the cypher and the operator's lettering belong, FLUSH reserved areas with no raised or cut geometry (canon owes them): no cypher, crown, operator lettering or maker's mark, the collection plate saying only COLLECTIONS, MON-FRI 5.30 PM, SAT 12 NOON, and the front facing the building line; no photograph of a pillar box was reached, so no number is Photo-measured: every size is the repository's earlier figures (Read), derived from them, or the writer's judgement, and the first dated photograph overrides them.

decision_type.main: Type A, 1950s-60s, cast iron, domed cap with a moulded rim, hooded aperture, a flush door; cypher, lettering and maker's mark reserved flush and blank

variant.why_a_variant_at_all: the earlier research (Read) says the capless Type K was introduced on 31 July 1980 and made to about 2000, so a few were in the street in 1990 as new or replacement boxes; two search-summary leads (not numbers) give it the same 19 1/4 in width
variant.why_not_built: the street needs one box; the research's own recommendation is the older Type A; and the evidence for the Type K's shape is two search summaries and no photograph, so no profile is offered beyond the coarse one below
variant.differences: no separate cap or overhanging rim; a flush rounded crown; the aperture set in a shallow recess rather than under a hood; the same 489 mm body and about the same height (Judgement; lead only)

reasons_for_main: 1990 on a Victorian port quarter: the stock is the older cast-iron standard boxes, not the 1980 capless replacement (the research says so, and recommends a 1950s-60s Type A: Read)
the stand-in already has a cap and a dome, so the silhouette the street was blocked with is the Type A's
the Type A's cap, hooded slot, door and plate give the sheet four things to show at the camera's 1.6 m; the capless box has fewer

the postal cypher and the operator lettering are what canon owes: on a Type A they have clear places to stay reserved and flush (a band, a disc); on a capless box they are cast into the aperture plate

scene.front_faces: the building line: the east (shop) side, away from the carriageway (review N6)
scene.front_direction_in_scene: +z on the east side (toward the shops); the stand-in's slot is on the road side (StreetVignette.cs PillarBox: z - sgn x 0.48 x d, Read), so the kit piece is turned 180 degrees about the vertical against the stand-in
scene.reason: the foot stands 312 mm from the kerb's back, so a road-facing slot would put the poster on the kerb edge or in the channel; a kerbside box on a 2 m footway faces the footway or along it; the player walks the footway and would otherwise see the box's plain back. Judgement (the reviewer's); the scene's road side is a Read figure against it: the scene owner is told (handover) and, if the road side is kept, records why

clear_footway_past_box_mm.note: 2000 - 600 - 288 = 1112 if 'the setback' is to the axis (the scene's code); 0.6 m to the NEAREST edge would put the axis at 888 and leave 824 (see could_not_settle)

nearest_lamp_column.note: the scene's east column at x = 28.0 stands 1.0 m from the box on the same setback: the lantern (5 m up, 0.5 m out) lights the cap from above and at night the box is the street's nearest object to a sodium lamp

upper_alternative_total_height.why: the research's untraced Type A, 5 ft 4 in tall (and 1 ft 7 1/4 in wide); the scene's stand-in (1612) agrees; a photograph settles 1500 against 1626

lower_range_not_used.why: the 73 in listing less 15 to 20 in buried is a casting's length, and a lead sells that box as the narrow Type B; the research's own Type A figures are 150 cm and 5 ft 4 in

profile.note: outer surface of the lathe, (radius, z) in mm, from the foot of the hidden skirt up to the apex; revolve about the axis. Hard edges get the bevels in `bevels`. The features that are not bodies of revolution (slot, hood, sill, door, escutcheon, plate frame) are in `parts`.
profile.inner_offset: the inside is the outer profile offset 12 mm inward, closed at z = -138 (for the section drawing; a closed solid is acceptable to the build apart from the slot)

bevels.edge: cap rim top and bottom lips

foot_plinth.what: the foot: a 48 mm vertical band at r 288 with a 12 mm quarter-round, a 45 degree splay and a cove into the body; the casting continues some 15 to 20 in deeper (the research); 150 mm of it is modelled as a hidden skirt

set_in_footway.datum: z = 0 is the footway surface at the box's axis
set_in_footway.hidden_skirt: profile segment buried_skirt to z = -150 so no gap shows where paving dips

fillet.how: an irregular ring of dark bitumen and mortar, 15 to 35 mm wide, 10 mm high at the foot, feathered to nothing on the paving; wider on the uphill (building) side because the footway falls 14 mm across the foot while the box stands vertical

set_in_footway.paving_cut: the flags are cut to a rough round, 20 to 60 mm from the foot, with a 5 to 12 mm gap the fillet covers (the footway family owns the flags)

body.what: plain cylinder with a sand-cast surface

surface.casting_seam: a 0.5 mm raised seam line down the back (x = 0, y < 0), where the two mould halves met

cap.what: the cap: an under-moulding (cove) from the body to a 280 rim, a vertical rim, a quarter-round bead, a flat shelf, a short neck and the shallow dome. The rim is the outermost line above the foot; the hood tucks inside it.
cap.finial: none (no boss, no ring): the earlier research names none (Read) and no photograph shows one

slot.through: yes: through the 12 mm wall into a black interior (albedo 8/8/8, roughness 0.9)
slot.kind: size Read (the scene's 320 x 45); centre Derived (the scene's 1150 + 128)

hood.what: a curved lip wrapped round the front above the slot

door.placement: a flush door concentric with the body: a cylindrical panel of outer radius 245.5 (1 mm proud of the body's 244.5), 300 wide as a chord (half angle 37.7 degrees), z 280 to 1168; only the 3 x 3 joint groove round it shows it
door.hinged: on the left as seen from the front, as the side of the joint only: the hinges are INTERNAL (a knocked-out pin must not open the box), so no knuckle, pin or strap shows; no part on the door's left edge stands more than 1.5 mm proud of the door face
door.face: plain, sand-cast, a thick-painted bead along its edges

lock.side: right (opposite the hinged side, where the joint line is)

reserved_for_lettering.placement: a flush reserved band on the body's own face (radius 244.5), concentric with the body, 300 wide as a chord (half angle 37.8 degrees) and 40 high; no raised or cut geometry at all; painted the surrounding red (the body's), with no tint, outline or mask in any texture: invisible on the built box
reserved_for_lettering.note: FLUSH: no raised or cut geometry (relief 0 within the area, measured radially above the body's own curved face), painted the surrounding red (the body's), with no tint, outline or mask in any texture: invisible on the built box. The minted lettering is cast here once canon supplies it.

reserved_for_cypher.placement: a flush reserved disc on the door's own face (radius 245.5), concentric with the door's face and centred on the door's axis, 110 across; no raised or cut geometry at all; painted the surrounding red (the door's), with no tint, outline or mask in any texture: invisible on the built box
reserved_for_cypher.note: FLUSH: no raised or cut geometry (relief 0 within the area, measured radially above the door's own curved face), painted the surrounding red (the door's), with no tint, outline or mask in any texture: invisible on the built box. The minted cypher is cast here once canon supplies it.

panels.note: a real box carries its cypher and lettering as raised letters directly on the iron: it has no blank disc and no blank tablet (review N5). Canon owes the postal cypher and the operator's name; the box is correct and incomplete.

collection_frame.form: flat-faced boss: its face plane is the plane y = 254.5 (9 above the door's face at the axis), its sides run back to the cylinder (33 proud at its edges)

collection_plate.face: white vitreous enamel (232,229,218), roughness 0.12, thin black border line 2 mm inset 4 mm

text.rule: a 1.5 mm black rule under the heading, 24 mm from the top, inset 14 mm each side

collection_plate.font: any plain grotesque already in production/fonts (OFL); not a period-correct face, none is needed at 8 mm

plates.enamel_plate: none: the box carries ONE plate (review N5); a blank enamel plate in a frame reads as a placeholder

words_decision.nowhere_else: no other letters or numerals appear on the box
words_decision.why_safe: they are the plain English words and times a collection plate needs; none names a company, brand, council, maker or reign, none is a cypher or a crown; 'POST OFFICE', 'ROYAL MAIL', 'LETTERS' on the slot, 'PO', 'GPO', 'ER' and any foundry name are NOT used. If the brand bible later wants zero lettering the text list is removed and the frame is removed with it (variant `no_plate`: a flush door; the self-check and the checks accept both).

red.name: pillar-box red, a deep gloss red (the colour of the box above the black band)
red.source: kept from the wear target: Read
red.roughness_words: semi-gloss: a gloss enamel five to eight years after its last repaint, dulled and a little chalked on the top of the cap (0.45) and brighter on the vertical faces (0.35)

black_base.edge: the line between black and red is a brush line, wavering +-3 mm, the red overlapping the black by 1 to 2 mm in places; it crosses the foot's cove and the lower body
black_base.kind: Read (the research: black, about 20 cm); a variant with no band is listed under variants

keyhole_shutter.note: painted with the door, worn to dark bare metal at its edge only (review N8: not bright brass); if a builder prefers brass it is Memory

wet.note: paint stays glossy; a water film darkens the diffuse by about 12 % and the highlights sharpen

naive_rgb_multiply.note: an RGB engine multiplies albedo by the lamp triple and keeps the red channel: the box stays a dark RED; a real 589 nm lamp can only make it a dark orange-olive brown

sodium.spectral_ratio_range_note: from the fitted edges (lower) to the same pigments with the edge 12 nm bluer (upper): a box about a tenth to a quarter as bright as a white surface; Judgement, the curve's shape is assumed

wear.state: tired: five to eight years since its last repaint, one tidy-up of the plate and the lock, no touch-up of the chips; the street is a port town's old quarter in a wet climate

agrees_with_wear_target.repeat_rule: the 214 mm strip does not fit the 1536 mm girth a whole number of times (7.2); an odd count cannot be mirrored closed, so 8 repeats of 192 mm (the strip 10 % narrower), mirrored on alternate repeats, the seam at the back (x = 0, y < 0)
agrees_with_wear_target.height: the mask runs from z = 0 up the 1500 mm of the box (the wear target's is 2.4 m; the lowest 0.3 m keeps its 40 % of the lost paint)
agrees_with_wear_target.disagreement: the wear target's 0.04 to 0.08 is the downpipe's; the box takes 0.03 to 0.06 (typical 0.04) because a box in service is touched up. The wear writer should accept or overrule.

layers_in_a_chip.description: a chip shows the layers of the repaints: the top red, an older red, then primer or bare iron; chips are hard-edged with a thick paint bead (0.3 to 0.6 mm) round them
layers_in_a_chip.kind: Judgement; the tone mark 124/104/92 of the wear target is the mean of primer and rust
layers_in_a_chip.nearest_evidence: a Poly Haven CC0 scan of a weathered red-painted container (rusty_painted_metal, published 2025): faded red 119/64/47 with run streaks that read 44/28/23 (a third of the red's luminance) over about 7 % of its area; a scan of a shipping container, NOT a pillar box, used only for how rust runs over red paint

chips_at_the_base.foot_top_edge_scuff: the quarter-round on the foot top (z 48 to 60) is worn to bare iron over 30 % of the circumference, a band 10 to 14 mm wide, colour 96/84/76, strongest on the road side (the back: kerb-side knocks from wheels and bags)

kerb_side_scrape.side: the road side (the back, 180 degrees from the front, which faces the shops)

sill_lip.note: letters scrape the lip bright; a dull dark iron band, not shiny

chips_at_the_aperture.slot_interior: black; a faint pale line where the flap's lip catches the light

micro_chips.on: door perimeter, hood edge, sill edge, cap rim lips, foot top edge, the keyhole shutter's edge

sources: the hood's underside, one trickle under its LEFT end

trickle.head: a dark dot at the source 3 to 10 mm and a 15 to 40 mm brown halo

rust_bleed.kind: Judgement; widths from the wear target's rust_bleed (Photo M14, a wall, not iron)

patches.where: on the sides and back, 70 to 140 degrees round from the front (never on the door, the plate, the lock, the slot or the hood)
patches.edges: torn on the diagonal, 2 to 10 mm hard edge
patches.content: unreadable remnants; nothing that shows a word, a face, a drink or a wager

flyposting_traces.cross_reference: the scene's G5 sticker decal (0.15 x 0.15 m on the street face at 0.15 m up) sits on the box's road side, which is now the back: keep it there, clear of the door

ground_up.note: the wear target's foot-splash envelope (full to 240, half at 450, gone by 750) applied to the box: multiplier = 1 - 0.38 x level on the red; the black band takes 0.8 x level

rain_streaks_from_the_cap_rim.effect: a cleaner, brighter streak (x 1.12) down a dirtier ground (the cap's overhang protects what is under it)

bird_droppings_on_the_dome.runs: 0 to 1 run of 10 to 30 mm wide, 50 to 300 long down the cap rim
bird_droppings_on_the_dome.place: the dome's top and the rim; the quay end gets more (the box stands at x 27: weight 0.4)

chalking.where: the top of the dome and the cap rim's upper face
chalking.effect: lighter and a little pink, x 1.08 in linear light, roughness 0.45

wear.first_look_at_1p6_m: from the game camera the eye should read: a red cylinder as tall as a man's shoulder, a dark grimy foot and black band, three or four orange-brown chip clusters low down, one dark rust trickle under the hood's left end, a torn paper remnant on the side, the bright white plate, the black slot

list.description: Type A, red body, black band, tired wear, the collection plate lettered with the five allowed strings

all red to the ground (a repaint that skipped the base); the black band's top z = 0; the evidence for the band in 1990 is the research's Read plus leads that a red-and-black-base livery was stipulated long before
no plate and no frame (a flush door), if canon wants no lettering at all: delete the collection frame and its plate; the reserved areas are unchanged

red_paint.name: pillar-box red, a deep gloss red (the colour of the box above the black band)
red_paint.source: kept from the wear target: Read
red_paint.roughness_words: semi-gloss: a gloss enamel five to eight years after its last repaint, dulled and a little chalked on the top of the cap (0.45) and brighter on the vertical faces (0.35)

black_paint.edge: the line between black and red is a brush line, wavering +-3 mm, the red overlapping the black by 1 to 2 mm in places; it crosses the foot's cove and the lower body
black_paint.kind: Read (the research: black, about 20 cm); a variant with no band is listed under variants

keyhole_shutter.note: painted with the door, worn to dark bare metal at its edge only (review N8: not bright brass); if a builder prefers brass it is Memory

bare_iron_and_rust.metal_note: bare iron is metal 1 but a rust skin is a dielectric; 0.3 on a chip that is mostly rust, 1.0 only on the bright sill band

bevels_note: every hard edge is bevelled (mid-poly, bevel on every edge: the asset plan's method, Read); the radii are in `bevels`

triangle_budget.kind: Judgement: the asset plan's mid-poly with a bevel on every edge (Read); the box fills at most 1 % of a frame beyond 8 m

accent_budget.note: art-direction R-B4: the red boxes are the street's whole high-chroma accent; the frame's pixels above saturation 0.6 must be non-zero and under 0.078
accent_budget.kind: Derived: area x (1440 / (2 d tan 23 degrees))^2 / 3.686 Mpx
accent_budget.wet_note: the sky's reflection lowers saturation on the cap's top and the highest bright patches to about 0.6 to 0.7; the body's vertical faces stay at 0.75 to 0.8

photographs_win.why: no photograph of a pillar box was reached, so no photograph overrides anything. The disagreements below are between the repository's own figures (and the reviewer's judgement); each says what was chosen.

disagreements.chosen: 489 for the body; the scene's 597 is read as the foot (576 chosen)

disagreements.b: the research's working figure 150 cm ('the top is at about 150 cm'), its Type A line 5 ft 4 in (1626), the scene's own stand-in 1612
disagreements.chosen: 1500 (Read: the research's working figure); 1626 recorded as the upper alternative; 1350 to 1470 is a casting's length (a lead says a Type B's) and is not used; the stand-in is 0.11 m too tall

disagreements.chosen: 560 (35.5 proud), the outermost line above the foot; the hood tucks 5.5 inside it

to_read_when_the_network_opens: dated photographs, 1975 to 2000, of Type A and Type B boxes of the 1950s-60s on provincial British streets, front, side and three-quarter, with a person or a kerb in frame for scale (Geograph, Wikimedia Commons categories of UK pillar boxes, Flickr archives of the 1980s, local archives such as Leodis, Picture Sheffield, Tyne and Wear and Hull History Centre); the one photograph that settles most is a dated, square-on front view of a Type A of the 1950s-60s with the kerb's 125 mm upstand or a standing person in frame, camera about 1 m up and 4 to 6 m away
the Letter Box Study Group's type records: Type A and Type K entries (heights, widths, the order of cypher, lettering and plates, apertures by date), and its notes on how the aperture changed in 1957

Royal Mail's and the Postal Museum's archives: repaint and paint specifications of the 1980s (the base band's height, the exact red), drawings of the standard boxes, the dimensions of the A and B castings
Historic England and Cadw listing records for listed Type A boxes (some give measured sizes)
a measured visit: a real Type A on a street near the PC, with a tape and a scale rod (the PC has the network the cloud lacks)
dated photographs of the Type K as new in the 1980s, to decide whether it needs a second variant

panorama_search.method: every British panorama listed by api.polyhaven.com/assets?type=hdris with coordinates in Britain was downloaded as its tone-mapped JPG (every one is 8192 px wide) and searched twice: (1) saturated-red blob detection on a 4096 px reduction (hue within 30 degrees of red, saturation above 0.68, value above 0.30), then every blob over 80 px was looked at as a rectilinear crop; (2) eight rectilinear views at 72 degrees across each street panorama, looked at by eye. Script: scan_panoramas.py. The reviewer re-ran a looser search (saturation above 0.45, value above 0.12, 40 px) on three of them and found no pillar box either.

catalogue.source: api.polyhaven.com/assets?type=hdris on 9 October 2026 (the writer's count of 997; the review's 732 with coordinates, so 265 without)

searched: leadenhall_market (red blobs only: a covered market's painted shopfronts)
left_out: docklands_01, docklands_02 and the other 2025 Poly Haven panoramas at 53.3 N, 6.2 W: Dublin, where boxes are green and Irish
the 265 Poly Haven panoramas with no coordinates (none labelled British; a pillar box abroad is not a British one)
panorama_search.result: NO PILLAR BOX in any of them. Every saturated-red blob was a tail light, a brick wall, a painted shopfront, a refuse bin or a sign. Poly Haven's 521 CC0 models include no pillar box, post box or letter box; its textures include none; ambientCG's catalogue has none.

red_blobs_checked.urban_street_02: a purple bin, brick, an orange barrier
red_blobs_checked.urban_street_03: tail lights of two parked cars, a brick wall

could_not_settle: whether a Type A of the 1950s-60s stands 1500 above the footway (the research's working figure, kept) or up to 1626 (5 ft 4 in, the research's untraced Type A line): a photograph beside a kerb (125) or a person settles it in a minute; read it FIRST
the slot's width: 320 is 65 % of the body's width (Read, the scene's); the reviewer's judgement is that a 1950s-60s Type A's slot is nearer half the body's width; read it SECOND, after the height

the real order and positions on the front of the cypher, the operator lettering, the collection plate and the lock; the reserved areas and the frame are placed by the writer's general knowledge (basis Memory) and each may be 40 mm or more out
the shape of the cap's moulding, the dome's rise (80 against the scene's 140) and the 30 mm neck, whether a finial or boss exists, and the hood's depth: not to be moved without a photograph
whether the front faces the building line (this target's choice, the reviewer's) or the carriageway (the scene's stand-in), and which side the door's joint is on
whether '0.6 m back from the kerb' is to the axis (the scene's code; kept) or to the nearest edge: it moves the box 0.29 m and the clear footway from 1112 to 824 mm
the exact 1990 red: pillar-box reds were BS 381C 538 or 539 (a lead); the sRGB 150/30/32 is the wear target's guess, kept, and is checked against the accent budget not against a paint chip
the base band's height (200 Read; 152 as a lead) and whether a 1990 repaint kept it
the Type K as a second variant: only worth writing once a dated photograph shows one in a street like this
a 'next collection' number tablet or rotary dial: not modelled (the research: uncertain)
the red's reflectance at 589 nm (6.5 of TARGET.md): a fitted edge gives 0.08, a bluer edge 0.12 to 0.20; a spectrum of the real paint would settle it

handover.for_scene_file: furniture E4: replace body 0.597 / 1.372, cap 0.660 x 0.100 and dome 0.140 with the kit piece (total height 1.500, foot 0.576, body 0.489, cap 0.560); its pivot is the axis at the footway; the stand-in (1.612 in all) was 0.11 m too tall. THE FRONT (door, slot, plate) FACES THE BUILDING LINE, 180 degrees from the stand-in, whose slot is on the road side (StreetVignette.cs PillarBox): tell the scene owner; if the road side is kept, record why
handover.for_kerbs_and_footway: the footway stands at +125 above the channel at the box's axis (110 at the kerb back, +15 for the fall); the box stands vertical on it; the flags are cut round the foot with a fillet (see parts.foot_plinth.set_in_footway)

checks.name: total_height

checks.name: pivot_and_datum
checks.measure: the pivot (origin) lies on the axis at z = 0 and the lowest vertex lies between z = -160 and z = -100
checks.kind: Read (brief: pivot at the base's centre on the ground)

checks.name: verticality
checks.measure: angle between the axis and the vertical, degrees
checks.kind: Derived (the box stands vertical on a footway that falls 14 mm across the foot)

checks.name: profile_silhouette
checks.measure: on the back half (y < 0, clear of the casting seam), the section's outline in the r-z plane against profile.outer_rz from z 0 to the apex: the largest nearest distance either way (every point of the outline to the profile, and every point of the profile to the outline, sampled every 0.5 mm along each), mm. A cap that is a plain disc, a foot without its quarter-round, splay and cove, a square bead or a chamfered cove fails; a correct build placed up to 1 mm high, a true-sphere dome and a 1.5 mm bevel on the rim's lip pass.

checks.name: cap_soffit_height

checks.name: door_proud

checks.name: door_joint
